sections.h2: Which Spencer County offices handle a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Three offices share a Spencer County bill, and all of them work from Taylorsville, the county seat. The Property Valuation Administration (PVA) sets the value, the sheriff collects the money, and the county clerk takes over any bill left open after April 15. The sheriff's own site says the office never assigns a value to any property in the county.

  • PVA, (502) 477-3207: values every parcel, takes homestead applications and answers questions about an assessment.
  • Sheriff, (502) 477-3200: mails the bills each October and collects for the state, the county, the school districts, and sometimes cities and special districts such as fire protection and libraries.
  • County attorney, (502) 477-3225: runs delinquent-tax collection from 7 West Main Street and assists the PVA when an assessment appeal reaches the local board.
  • County clerk, 2 West Main Street: holds certificates of delinquency and accepts payment on any that have not been sold.

A bill that looks too high is a PVA question, and the time to ask is before the check goes out. The sheriff can only collect what the PVA's value and the local tax rates produce.

sections.h2: What should a Spencer County seller know about the area?
sections.html:
Spencer County covers 192 square miles, 187 of them land, and borders Jefferson County to the northwest. The legislature formed it in January 1824 from parts of Bullitt, Shelby and Nelson counties and named it for Captain Spier Spencer, who died at the Battle of Tippecanoe. Taylorsville became the seat that December and was incorporated in 1829. Elk Creek is the only census-designated place, and Kentucky 44 and Kentucky 55 are the main highways. Spencer County Public Schools runs six schools, among them Spencer County High School, Hillview Academy and Taylorsville Elementary.

The county counts as part of the Louisville/Jefferson County metropolitan area, and Taylorsville Lake, which lies mostly inside the county line, is described as a major local economic resource. Growth has been steep: 6,801 residents in 1990, 11,766 in 2000, 17,061 in 2010 and 19,490 in 2020. The Census Bureau estimate for July 2025 is 20,998.

A seller here is working with a bill built on a median home value of $330,000, the highest of the four counties in this set.

sections.h2: When is a Spencer County tax bill due, and what does paying late cost?
sections.html:
The bill is mailed on October 1 and is due by December 31, with a discount for paying early. Kentucky's collection statute sets four stages, and the sheriff's office follows the same ladder.

  • Through November 1: pay 2 percent less than the face amount.
  • November 2 through December 31: pay the face amount.
  • January 1 through January 31: a 5 percent penalty applies.
  • After January 31: the penalty becomes 10 percent.

The sheriff's collection page lists the February 1 to April 15 stage as 21 percent, which reflects the 10 percent penalty plus the sheriff's 10 percent add-on fee. Bills the sheriff has not collected by the close of business on April 15 move to the county clerk. If a mortgage company escrows your taxes, the bill itself tells you what to do, so check that the lender actually paid before the January penalty starts.

sections.h2: What happens to a Spencer County bill that goes delinquent?
sections.html:
Once the clerk receives it, the bill becomes a certificate of delinquency and a lien is recorded on the real estate under KRS 134.122. The county attorney's office describes the debt as personal to whoever owned the property on the January 1 assessment date, and says interest runs at 12 percent a year, added monthly. Penalties and fees stack on top.

After 90 days unpaid, outside buyers may purchase the certificate. Spencer County's first offering is usually a tax bill sale in August or September. A certificate cannot be sold while the owner has a payment agreement with the county attorney or while the property is tied up in foreclosure or bankruptcy litigation that the county attorney is part of. The county attorney tries to notify the owner by regular mail before a sale.

  • Not yet sold: pay the full amount plus accrued interest at the county clerk's office, 2 West Main Street.
  • Already sold: contact the purchaser, who sets the payment terms and may add substantial administrative costs.
  • Payment plan: the county attorney offers plans of roughly 4 to 8 months, which must be finished before the next tax bill comes due. Sign up through the online form, at (502) 477-3225, or in person, ideally by appointment. A certificate already sold to a purchaser does not qualify.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Spencer County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with a conference at the PVA's office, because Kentucky does not let an owner skip that step. The roll is open to public view for thirteen days beginning the first Monday in May. After a conference, the written appeal goes to the county clerk and must arrive by the close of business on the day after the inspection period ends.

The local board of assessment appeals sits 25 to 35 days after inspection closes and meets for no more than five days. It expects documents: sales of similar homes, an appraisal, repair estimates, insurance policies or listings. An appeal without them is denied, and an owner who never files locally cannot go on to the Kentucky Claims Commission. If bills are printed before the dispute ends, they use the value you claimed, and a supplemental bill follows when the board lands higher.

The PVA must physically inspect every parcel at least once every four years, and values can change annually. Ask the PVA for the list of sales behind your number; it is the quickest way to see whether the comparison homes match yours.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the Spencer County homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Homeowners aged 65 or older, and owners classified as totally disabled, can deduct a fixed sum from the assessed value of the home they live in. The Department of Revenue set that sum at $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 tax periods and recalculates it every two years. On a $200,000 home, tax would be computed on $150,900.

  • You must own, occupy and maintain the home as your residence on January 1.
  • File Form 62A350 with the Spencer County PVA by December 31 of the tax year.
  • Once accepted, the exemption continues for later years while the original applicant owns and lives there.
  • A buyer must file a new application, because the benefit follows the owner and not the house.

sections.h2: How are unpaid taxes handled when a Spencer County house sells?
sections.html:
Taxes for a year are the personal debt of the person who owned the property on January 1, and a delinquent-tax lien stays attached to the parcel for eleven years no matter who owns it afterward. A buyer therefore wants any open bill cleared at closing. Ask the sheriff for a payoff figure on the current year and ask the county clerk whether any certificate of delinquency exists, then confirm whether an outside purchaser holds it.

If a payment agreement with the county attorney is in place, tell the buyer's closing agent early, since the remaining balance has to be accounted for in the payoff. The same three offices supply every figure a closing agent needs.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a Spencer County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Pay the sheriff's office, which you can reach at (502) 477-3200. The county attorney's page says current-year bills can be looked up through the sheriff's site under the Property Taxes tab, and the bill is payable there until April 15, after which it moves to the clerk.

faqs.q: What if I miss the April 15 cutoff in Spencer County?
faqs.a: The unpaid bill goes to the county clerk as a certificate of delinquency with a recorded lien, and interest of 12 percent a year starts to build. After 90 days it can be bought by an outside purchaser, so call the county attorney early about a plan.

faqs.q: Can I get a payment plan for an overdue Spencer County bill?
faqs.a: Yes, if the certificate has not been sold. The county attorney's plans generally run 4 to 8 months and must end before the next bill is due. Call (502) 477-3225 or use the online form.

faqs.q: How much is the Spencer County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The state maximum is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 tax periods. You must be 65 or older, or totally disabled, and apply with the PVA by December 31 of the tax year.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay Spencer County back taxes before I can sell?
faqs.a: You can list the house, but the lien stays on the property until the tax is paid. Settle the payoff at closing, and request figures from the sheriff and the county clerk before you set a closing date.
